# Foundation Repair Advocate

> Independent, paid foundation second opinions and floor elevation surveys for Arizona homeowners. We are not a foundation repair contractor and do not sell piers, drainage systems, or structural repair — we provide measured documentation and a practical opinion so homeowners have the full picture before they sign a repair contract.

Foundation Repair Advocate serves Show Low, the White Mountains, Pinetop-Lakeside, Payson, Flagstaff, and the Phoenix metro area by appointment. Contact: (928) 298-5756.

## Core pages

- [Home](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/): Overview of the independent second-opinion service and who it's for.
- [What you get](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/what-you-get/): The floor elevation survey, on-site walkthrough, written guidance, and contractor questions included.
- [Why hire us](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/why-us/): How a paid independent opinion differs from free inspections, repair-company surveys, and engineering firms.
- [How it works](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/how-it-works/): The process — floor plan scan, scheduled visit, survey, written report, optional 12-month resurvey.
- [Service area](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/service-area/): Arizona coverage area and appointment availability.
- [Scope & disclosure](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/disclosure/): What is and is not provided — informational surveys and guidance, not engineering stamps or repair contracts.
- [Contact](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/contact/): How to reach Foundation Repair Advocate.

## Guides

- [Arizona expansive soils and drainage](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/guides/expansive-soils/): Why controlling water is often the highest-leverage first step before structural repair.
- [What a floor elevation survey shows](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/guides/floor-elevation-survey/): How to read a floor contour map and its limits.
- [Free inspection vs paid independent survey](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/guides/free-vs-paid/): Incentive and pressure differences between free and paid evaluations.
- [When monitoring beats installing piers](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/guides/monitoring/): When a documented baseline and watch list is the smarter first step.
- [Questions to ask a repair contractor](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/guides/questions-to-ask/): Practical questions to ask before signing a repair contract.
- [Reading a foundation repair bid](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/guides/reading-a-bid/): Pier count, methods, language, and red flags in repair proposals.
- [Foundation concerns before listing or during inspection](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/guides/real-estate/): Independent measurement for real estate transactions.
- [Should I get a second opinion?](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/guides/second-opinion/): When a second opinion on a repair estimate is worth it.
- [Settlement vs heave](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/guides/settlement-vs-heave/): How Arizona's expansive soils produce both, and why they're treated differently.
- [Foundation issues in the White Mountains & Show Low area](https://foundationrepairadvocate.com/guides/white-mountains/): Local soil patterns and regional guidance.

## Notes

- All guides and pages are informational. Foundation Repair Advocate does not diagnose structural adequacy, design repairs, or provide stamped engineering.
